title: It is written (Matthew 4:1–11)
hook: each answer to the tempter comes from Deuteronomy
tomorrow: where does a light start, if not in the capital?

segments.voice: Yesterday Jesus waited his turn at the river, and a voice said, this is my beloved Son. Your line: in line with sinners.

Late, the house asleep, and the thought sounds very reasonable: one more, you deserve it, nobody will know. Temptation doesn't have to sound like a villain. It can even quote scripture. Right after the river, Matthew says, the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness "to be tempted of the devil." Forty days without food, and afterward he was hungry. Then: "If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread."
screen: `IT SOUNDS REASONABLE.` → `FORTY DAYS, HUNGRY.` → `MAKE THESE STONES BREAD.`

segments.voice: Three tests, and every answer starts the same way. Bread first: "It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God." Then the tempter sets him on a pinnacle of the temple and quotes scripture himself, a psalm promising angels will catch you so you won't dash your foot against a stone. Go on, jump. Jesus: "It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God." Then a high mountain, all the kingdoms of the world, offered for one act of worship. "Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve." All three answers come from one book, Deuteronomy, Moses' words to Israel in the wilderness, where God let the people hunger and fed them manna, so they'd learn that "man doth not live by bread only." Now the part that matters on an ordinary Tuesday night. Jesus never argues with the tempter's logic, and he never improvises something clever. It is written isn't a password, either. The devil quotes scripture too. What holds is a line already lived with, there before the pull arrives, the way Jesus answered a wilderness with Israel's own wilderness lessons.
screen: `BREAD: NOT BY BREAD ALONE.` · `THE DEVIL QUOTES A PSALM.` · `THE MOUNTAIN: GOD ONLY.` · `ALL FROM DEUTERONOMY.` · then, large: `IT IS WRITTEN.`

segments.voice: Pick one short line that answers a pull you know well: man shall not live by bread alone, or a line from a source you trust. Say it out loud, slowly, five times, until it starts to stay, and then let it ride quietly on the breath.
It is written. Jesus' answer to the tempter, three times over, each one a line from Deuteronomy.
Your line: it is written. The tempter knew the words too; Jesus lived by them. Take care.

fork.setup: your group chat dares you to post something cruel about a classmate. someone adds, "come on, it's just a joke." what would answering like Jesus look like?

chat.meaning: Each of Jesus' answers starts 'it is written' and comes from Deuteronomy, words he lived by. The devil quoted a psalm too; the line has to be yours.

Deuteronomy.meaning: a book of Moses' words to Israel in the wilderness

manna.meaning: the food God gave Israel in the wilderness

pinnacle.meaning: a high point at the top of the temple

Satan.meaning: a name for the tempter, the devil

notes: The three answers trace to Deuteronomy 8:3, 6:16 and 6:13; confirm. The devil's quotation (Matthew 4:6) is from Psalm 91:11–12, paraphrased.
'Forty days and forty nights' is from Matthew 4:2 itself. The Israel parallel (hunger, testing, manna) rests on Deuteronomy 8:2–3; the voice doesn't give the count of Israel's years.
'Deuteronomy, the words of Moses to Israel in the wilderness' follows Deuteronomy 1:1.
Index hook says 'each answer to the tempter comes from Deuteronomy'; the voice says 'All three answers come from one book'. Matthew doesn't name the book; the attribution is by the parallel verses.
